detail.text: Root cause found: `GET /{slug}` makes every unknown path "named", so the foundation's store-handback (`maybeCloseStore`) never runs again and `TestNewOpensStoreAndServes` fails. The mux can't distinguish an unknown slug from a mistyped API path, so this needs a design decision only the plan's author has.

detail.reason:
The agent asks: Card redirect-stats: how should GET /<slug> be registered so it does not disable the foundation's store hand-back? Options: (a) allow this card one small edit to internal/server/server.go that keeps maybeCloseStore working with a root wildcard; (b) tell me to leave TestNewOpensStoreAndServes failing and let the integration card fix server.go; (c) something else.
Why: The card requires a route at GET /{slug}. ServeMux then matches every unknown path under /, including the mistyped API paths the foundation test uses (/api/me, /api/nothing-here, POST /api/links). Server.named() therefore always returns true, Auth never calls s.maybeCloseStore(), and the existing acceptance test TestNewOpensStoreAndServes (auth_test.go:165) fails: after srv.Close() the database's -wal and -shm files remain, because nothing ever closes the store New opened for itself. The feature itself works: TestRedirect, TestRedirectUnknown, TestStats, TestStatsAfterClicks plus auth and cross-user cases all pass with -race. I cannot fix it inside routes_redirect.go alone: any catch-all under / has the same effect, and no pattern can distinguish an unknown slug from a mistyped API path once both live on the same mux. The card's directories are internal/server, but its brief implies only routes_redirect.go and its test file may change, and .forgejo/ is fixed.
Recommendation: Take option (a): let this card make the handler own the fallback instead of Auth's routing guess, which is 3 lines in server.go and leaves auth_test.go untouched. In New, drop the guard around the close call (Auth currently does `if s.mux != nil && !s.named(...)`), and register the last root pattern as the closer and 404 answer:

    s.register("GET /", http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
        s.maybeCloseStore()
        writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound)
    }))

ServeMux prefers the more specific patterns (GET /{slug}, GET /{$}, /app/, /healthz), so this subtree pattern only receives what nothing else matched, and the store is handed back exactly where the redirect card's 404 answers. It also makes named()/probe() unnecessary for this purpose, which the integration card can then simplify. If you prefer no edit outside routes_redirect.go, say so and I will instead leave TestNewOpensStoreAndServes red for the integration card, or move the two redirect tests into package server where they do not depend on the store being closed. Either way the redirect and stats handlers themselves need no change.
